title: Due Diligence, Investigation & Forensic Accounting
outcomes: Plan and report due diligence reviews.
Conduct investigations and distinguish them from audits.

meta.exam_tip: Identify the client and decision — that defines the investigation's focus.

concepts.title: Due diligence: types, approach and report
body: Due diligence is an investigation of a business before a transaction (acquisition, merger, investment, lending) to confirm facts, find risks and support valuation and negotiation.

Types: financial, tax, legal, commercial/operational, human resources, IT, environmental and others. Financial due diligence examines quality of earnings, working capital, net debt, contingent liabilities, projections and accounting policies.

Approach: agree scope, obtain data room information, analyse, interview management, and report. The report contains executive summary, scope and limitations, key findings and deal issues, quality of earnings adjustments, and recommendations for price or protections.
concepts.analogy: Due diligence turns a seller's story into verified facts.
concepts.work: Normalising earnings removes one-off gains before valuation.

concepts.title: Investigation: nature, steps and audit compared
body: Investigation is a critical, in-depth examination of records for a specific purpose (fraud, valuation, loan, partnership), often with no fixed scope, unlike an audit which gives an opinion on statements under standards.

Steps: define objective and scope; plan; gather and examine evidence (documents, interviews, analytics); evaluate findings; report facts with supporting evidence — the investigator reports facts, not opinions beyond the mandate.
Special issues: investigation period, reliance on audited statements, legal considerations, confidentiality, and need for experts.
concepts.analogy: Audit opines on statements; investigation finds facts for a purpose.
concepts.work: A lender's investigation focuses on repayment capacity and security.

concepts.title: Types of investigation
body: Investigations for an incoming partner (profit trend, maintainable profit, deed terms, liabilities), for valuation of shares in private companies (maintainable profit, assets, restrictions), for a bank or financial institution considering a loan (purpose, financial position, management, security, cash flows), and for a buyer of a business.
Fraud investigations: misappropriation of cash or goods, manipulation of accounts, fictitious payroll, purchase frauds; review of profit forecasts.
Each type adjusts focus and procedures to the client's decision.
concepts.analogy: Same skills, different questions for each client.
concepts.work: A bank asks: can the borrower repay and is the security adequate?

concepts.title: Forensic accounting and investigation standards
body: Forensic accounting applies accounting, auditing and investigative skills to legal matters — fraud detection, disputes, insolvency, valuation for litigation — producing evidence that can withstand court scrutiny.

Process: initial meeting and scoping, planning, evidence collection (documents, digital forensics, data analytics, interviews), analysis (including Benford's law, trend and ratio analysis), reporting and possibly expert testimony.

ICAI's Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards (FAIS) guide engagements: independence and objectivity, engagement acceptance, planning, evidence gathering and documentation, using experts, and reporting. Forensic professionals need skepticism, legal awareness and confidentiality.
concepts.analogy: Forensic work must be evidence-grade for courts.
concepts.work: Data analytics flags vendors sharing bank accounts with employees.

Quality of earnings and contingent exposures.

viva.model: An independent examination of a business before a transaction to verify facts, identify risks and support valuation.
Audit gives an opinion on statements under standards with a defined scope; investigation is a purpose-specific in-depth examination reporting facts.

viva.q: What does a bank's investigation cover?
viva.model: The purpose of the loan, the borrower's financial position and management, cash flows for repayment and adequacy of security.
Applying accounting and investigative skills to produce evidence for legal matters such as fraud and disputes.

viva.q: Name stages of a forensic engagement.
viva.model: Scoping, planning, evidence collection, analysis, reporting and expert testimony.
